successCriteria.description: The LeaveBalance entity exposes exactly the canonical fields (id, employeeId, policyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays, fiscalYear, status, createdAt, updatedAt) with status typed as the union 'ACTIVE' | 'CLOSED' | 'FORECAST', and imports Employee and LeavePolicy types from their module entry points for FK reference typing.

ILeaveBalanceRepository declares all required operations: findById, findByEmployeeId, findByEmployeeAndPolicy, findByEmployeeAndFiscalYear, save, update, and incrementUsedDays — and PgLeaveBalanceRepository implements that interface.

incrementUsedDays accepts an optional client parameter as its last argument; when the client is provided the increment query executes on that client (the caller's open transaction), and when omitted it falls back to the shared pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts (auto-commit).

incrementUsedDays performs the increment atomically in a single statement that both adds the delta to used_days and recomputes remaining_days = total_entitlement - used_days, and rejects (throws a typed error) any positive increment that would make used_days exceed total_entitlement.

incrementUsedDays accepts a negative delta to restore balance (for reversal of a previously-approved request) and correctly decrements used_days / recomputes remaining_days without throwing when the result stays within [0, total_entitlement].
save rejects a duplicate (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear) tuple with a typed error, enforcing one balance row per employee per policy per fiscal year.

Jest unit tests exist under tests/unit/modules/leave-balance/ covering the model field shape, every repository read/write operation, the client-provided vs client-omitted execution paths for incrementUsedDays, the entitlement-ceiling rejection, and negative-delta restoration.

constraints: All database access goes through the repository pattern (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository); the repository must obtain its connection from src/shared/db/connection.ts and must not be bypassed by inline SQL elsewhere.
Strict TypeScript: no implicit any, strict null checks (HARNESS.json no-any rule) — use unknown with type guards instead of any for row mapping.

Modules import from each other ONLY through their declared public entry point (index.ts); leave-balance must import Employee and LeavePolicy types via ../employee and ../leave-policy, never from internal files.

remaining_days is a materialized/computed value equal to total_entitlement - used_days (binding materialized-balance rule); it must never be set independently of that formula on save, update, or incrementUsedDays.
No circular dependencies: leave-balance depends on employee and leave-policy (per the reconciled dependency map) but neither of those modules may import leave-balance.
No hardcoded secrets (HARNESS.json no-hardcoded-secrets); the repository must source the connection string from the shared pool, not inline credentials.
outOfScope: LeaveBalance service, controller, and routes — balance is read/written internally by the LeaveRequest service in Phase 8/9; no HTTP surface is built in this phase.

Business-day counting utility and leave-request balance deduction workflow — the actual deduction-on-approval unit of work is owned by the LeaveRequest service in Phase 9; this phase only provides the atomic incrementUsedDays primitive.
Balance accrual scheduling / BullMQ background jobs and fiscal-year rollover logic.
Audit logging of balance mutations (GP-002) — audit records are emitted by the LeaveRequest service layer in Phase 10, not by the repository in this phase.
Database migrations / DDL for the leave_balances table — this phase assumes the table exists per the reconciled SQL schema; it does not create migrations.

ambiguities.description: The existing incrementUsedDays unit test asserts the exact SQL string and the two-call (findById + UPDATE) sequence. Adding the optional client parameter changes the execution path (query runs on client.query vs pool.query when a client is supplied), so the existing test's mock setup (which only mocks pool.query) and its exact-SQL assertion will break. The code agent must update the test to mock both pool.query and client.query paths rather than preserving the current assertion verbatim.
options: Update the existing test to mock both pool.query (client omitted) and client.query (client provided) execution paths, relaxing the exact-SQL assertion to a stringContaining check
Keep the exact-SQL assertion but add a separate test case for the client-provided path that mocks client.query
Rewrite the incrementUsedDays test suite from scratch to cover both paths without asserting the literal SQL

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeaveBalance row is unique per (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear); at most one balance exists for a given employee, policy, and fiscal year.

remainingDays is always equal to totalEntitlement - usedDays; it is a derived/materialized value and must be recomputed whenever usedDays or totalEntitlement changes (on save, update, and incrementUsedDays).
usedDays must remain within [0, totalEntitlement]; an increment that would push usedDays above totalEntitlement is rejected, and usedDays must never go negative.
status lifecycle is ACTIVE (drawable) → CLOSED (historical); FORECAST is a future-year balance that is not yet drawable. Only ACTIVE balances are eligible for usedDays increments.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws a typed error when a positive delta would make used_days exceed total_entitlement; returns null when the balance id does not exist. Must execute atomically — the used_days increment and remaining_days recompute occur in a single statement so no intermediate state is observable.
Throws a typed error on a duplicate (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear) tuple; persists and returns the balance with remainingDays recomputed as totalEntitlement - usedDays.
Returns null when the balance id does not exist; on success recomputes remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays and refreshes updatedAt.
Pure read operations; return null (single-result) or empty array (multi-result) when no rows match. No state mutation.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeaveBalance entity shape must match the reconciled canonical attributes exactly (id, employeeId, policyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays, fiscalYear, status 'ACTIVE'|'CLOSED'|'FORECAST', createdAt, updatedAt) and the materialized-balance business rule (remaining_days = total_entitlement - used_days; deduction on approval via atomic increment).

The repository must obtain its pooled connection from the shared pool exported here; the optional-client fallback path uses this same pool, and the client type must be compatible with the node-postgres PoolClient so Phase 9 can pass a pool.connect() client through.

Employee type for the employeeId FK reference must be imported via the employee module's public entry point (../employee), matching the existing index.ts re-export pattern, not from internal model files.
LeavePolicy type for the policyId FK reference must be imported via the leave-policy module's public entry point (../leave-policy), matching the existing index.ts re-export pattern.

The leave-balance module's public entry point must re-export the LeaveBalance entity, the LeaveBalanceStatus type, the ILeaveBalanceRepository interface, and the PgLeaveBalanceRepository class, matching the existing sibling-module index.ts convention so downstream phases import only through index.ts.

The repository implementation pattern (interface + Pg*Repository class, pool.query usage, private mapRow helper casting Record<string, unknown> to the entity, snake_case column mapping) must be consistent with the established Employee and LeavePolicy repositories.

integrationPoints.why: leave-balance depends on Employee for the employeeId foreign-key reference typing; imported via the employee module entry point per the reconciled dependency map.
leave-balance depends on LeavePolicy for the policyId foreign-key reference typing; imported via the leave-policy module entry point per the reconciled dependency map.

The repository uses the shared pool for auto-commit queries and accepts an optional PoolClient so Phase 9's LeaveRequest service can pass its open transaction client to incrementUsedDays for atomic balance deduction.

incrementUsedDays is the atomic primitive the Phase 9 leave-request approval/rejection/cancellation workflow calls within its unit-of-work transaction (BEGIN → status update + incrementUsedDays on the same client → COMMIT/ROLLBACK). The optional-client signature is the contract this phase delivers for that consumer.
